Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.
The extraction-only visual limitation was addressed by inspecting every PDF page and all ten figures and nine tables; six final original crops were also inspected.

Identity/version scope: the title page identifies arXiv:2607.23969v2, 30 Jul 2026. Title and eleven authors match the catalog; the catalog affiliation string omits the verified Leapmotor affiliation. Earlier revisions and a revision history were not supplied, so changes between versions cannot be established.
No separate supplement was supplied. Linked code, checkpoints and datasets were not inspected; no experiment was reproduced.

synopsis: LeapBot-WA trains a manipulation policy with future semantic guidance, then executes actions using a cache of the current observation. Its V-JEPA features pass through an isotropy-regularized semantic autoencoder before asymmetric world/action training. Reported simulation performance is competitive, especially against the listed latent WAMs, but the supplied v2 contains unresolved objective, pretraining and numerical inconsistencies. The architectural idea is clearer than the exact reproducible recipe. [e-overview, e-cache, e-isae, e-libero, e-objective-conflict]

problem.text: The authors argue that reconstructing textures, lighting and backgrounds can distract robot policies from physical state transitions. Their proposed solution is to predict in a pretrained semantic space and transfer that training signal into an action policy. This motivates the design; it does not establish that all pixel-generating policies waste capacity or that Gaussian isotropy is universally necessary for diffusion.

contributions.text: ISAE reconstructs predictive features while regularizing their latent distribution; camera identity is introduced downstream, allowing shared encoding across views.
Separate semantic and action transformers interact asymmetrically during training. Deployment retains semantic conditioning but bypasses future dynamics rollout.

inputs: Language instruction and current proprioceptive state
Training only: demonstrated action sequences and future semantic targets
outputs: A continuous action chunk for receding-horizon execution
Training only: semantic predictions/velocity estimates, with conflicting loss definitions disclosed below

steps.name: Encode and compress
steps.detail: V-JEPA 2.1 converts each resized 384×384 frame into 576 tokens of width 1664. The shared ISAE samples a Gaussian latent of width 96 per token and reconstructs features, without pixel decoding.

steps.name: Restore view identity
steps.detail: Add a learned camera residual after projecting normalized noisy latents. Semantic tokens use spatiotemporal 3D RoPE; action tokens use temporal 1D RoPE.

steps.name: Transfer future semantics into action learning
steps.detail: The intent-conditioned Anchor DiT cannot read target action tokens. The Action DiT reads both semantic and action tokens, while both branches attend to language/proprioception. This is auxiliary predictive guidance; the source's inverse-controller analogy does not specify a separate executed inverse-dynamics planner.

training.text: The three-stage account first adapts V-JEPA through LoRA and masked prediction, then freezes the adapted encoder to train ISAE, then freezes both encoders for world/action training. It describes five-source robot data, 7:3 external/wrist sampling, two-second windows and separate 7-/14-DoF action heads. The shorter implementation section covers only the last two stages.

Table 7 specifies 200k ISAE and 400k policy steps, AdamW at 1e-4, batch 256, bf16 and noise shift 5.0; the main text reports 24 H200 GPUs. The semantic DiT inherits Wan2.2-TI2V-5B weights. These pretrained components qualify claims of avoiding video or robot pretraining.

The training objective is unresolved: Table 7 uses unit action/semantic velocity losses and zero extra future loss; p. 12 instead gives action/JEPA weights 1/0.1 with SmoothL1; p. 13 gives 0.1/1; Table 9 uses future weight 0.2. These are not interchangeable recipes.

inference.text: Encode the current observation once and reuse its semantic keys/values throughout action denoising. Execute the first R actions of the predicted horizon H, then observe again. Future semantic generation is removed, but visual encoding, cache formation and action denoising remain; 'zero-overhead' is therefore an author characterization of the removed dynamics branch.

equations.explanation: Reconstruction combines squared feature error and weighted cosine distance; KL pulls the posterior toward a standard Gaussian; SIGReg penalizes departures from isotropy across random projections. Beta and lambda_iso weight the regularizers. The paper does not supply all numerical weights.

For concatenated semantic then action tokens, rows are queries and columns are keys. N_s and N_a count semantic and action tokens. Adding M to attention logits blocks semantic queries from action keys while preserving the reverse direction.

Here z and a are clean semantic and action sequences; epsilon_z and epsilon_a are independent standard Gaussian noise; t is the shared diffusion timestep. The detailed flow formulation targets velocities epsilon_z−z and epsilon_a−a. Later appendix losses conflict with this account.

results.setting: 50 simulated tasks; 27.5K mixed demonstrations; Table 8 states 100 trials per task/condition.
results.interpretation: Best randomized result among listed WAMs, not best overall average. Table 8 agrees for LeapBot-WA but changes baselines; its prose gives conflicting 92.64/89.80 values.

results.setting: 40 tasks; expert-trajectory training; stated aggregation over 2,000 episodes.
results.value: Table 2: Spatial 96.2; Object 99.6; Goal 97.6; LIBERO-10 95.6; average 97.3.
results.comparison: JEPA-VLA 96.4; VLA-JEPA 96.1; PALM 94.5; Lingbot-VA and Cosmos-Policy 98.5 average.
results.interpretation: Leads the listed latent WAMs. The accompanying 97.1% prose is inconsistent; retain the table's 97.3%. No uncertainty is reported.

results.setting: Transfer to systematic perturbations after expert-trajectory training; use the paper's stated 40-task/2,000-episode protocol.
results.interpretation: Strong improvement over listed latent baselines, with substantial camera/noise weakness and a remaining gap to the best listed pixel WAM.

results.setting: Table 4 LIBERO ablation; relationship to the main Table 2 configuration is unspecified.
results.value: Baseline 89.4/74.2; Robot-Mix 91.2/81.0; ISAE without SIGReg 91.4/80.2; full 92.0/85.0.
results.comparison: Adding SIGReg yields +0.6 average and +4.8 LIBERO-10 percentage points, but Goal falls 92.4→89.2.
results.interpretation: Supports a task-dependent benefit, not universal improvement or proof of isotropic geometry; no seed variation is given.

results.setting: Table 9 LIBERO comparison with semantic context held present.
results.interpretation: Future supervision adds a reported 1.3 average and 6.6 long-horizon percentage points. Loss-definition conflicts limit exact reproduction.

results.setting: Figure 4; matched inference hardware, horizon and denoising settings are unspecified.
results.metric: Reported model size and inference latency
results.interpretation: Smaller than Fast-WAM but slower in this chart. The plot supports neither universally fastest execution nor a fully controlled efficiency comparison.

results.setting: Base JEPA versus mixed-domain adaptation; probe split/training details unspecified.
results.interpretation: Features improve on the reported probes; this does not independently establish causal physical understanding.

limitations.text: Foundation-model representation quality limits fine contact physics and high-frequency tactile interactions; longer-horizon planning remains future work.

UR5 execution is shown qualitatively, without trial denominators or controlled success rates. Selected simulation images likewise cannot verify claimed attention shifts, invariance or absence of memorization.

The 'no embodied pretraining' table label is difficult to reconcile with the robot-corpus adaptation and cross-embodiment training account. No pixel reconstruction loss is used in the described policy training, but Wan video-model initialization remains. Dataset overlap and the origin of each reported checkpoint are unresolved.

Appendix Table 8 omits many task rows and contradicts its prose, including claims of perfect task success. Ablations peak below the main LIBERO score without a documented configuration bridge. These reporting gaps prevent pooling results into one consistent experimental record.

reproduction.text: Required ingredients include V-JEPA 2.1, adapted LoRA weights, ISAE, transferred Wan weights, robot demonstrations, frozen T5 conditioning and embodiment-specific action heads. Table 7 supplies optimizer and duration details, but the loss/checkpoint association must first be resolved.

Missing essentials include a complete data manifest and split/overlap accounting, LoRA rank/duration, ISAE loss weights, action normalization, denoising count, numeric H/R, cache projections and software versions. A meaningful first check would hold data and checkpoint initialization fixed while toggling future supervision and SIGReg separately.

reasoning.text: Distinct Anchor and Action DiTs support Dual-system even though they are jointly trained. Other mechanisms / Outside quadrants fits training-time semantic guidance with a static observation cache at deployment: future/action denoising occurs during learning, but execution is neither joint future rollout nor an explicit inverse-dynamics pipeline. The latent/JEPA category is well supported; efficiency is conditional on the incomplete timing protocol.

discussionQuestions: Which objective and training-data mixture produced each reported checkpoint? [e-objective-conflict, e-stages]
Does SIGReg improve physical prediction or primarily optimization stability when reconstruction quality is controlled? [e-isae, e-components]

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title, author/affiliation block and arXiv margin
evidence.detail: Title matches the supplied catalog; all eleven authors agree. The margin reads arXiv:2607.23969v2 [cs.RO], 30 Jul 2026. Affiliation 3 is Leapmotor, alongside the two HKUST institutions and Southeast University.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–2, Abstract, Introduction and Related Work
evidence.detail: The authors motivate predictive semantic alignment by arguing that visual reconstruction spends capacity on appearance and couples world generation to execution.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Figure 1 and Framework Overview, Eq. (1)
evidence.detail: Multi-view observations pass through V-JEPA and ISAE; language and proprioception form shared context. Anchor and Action DiTs exchange semantic guidance during training.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 3–4, Diffusion-Friendly Semantic Autoencoding, Figure 2, Eqs. (2)–(7)
evidence.detail: A Gaussian posterior compresses JEPA tokens; reconstruction combines squared error and cosine distance. KL regularization and SIGReg encourage Gaussian, isotropic latents. Figure 2 distinguishes frozen JEPA from trainable semantic encoder/decoder.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, View-Aware Residual Conditioning, Eq. (8)
evidence.detail: A learned camera embedding is added after normalization and projection of noisy semantic tokens at each denoising step, separately from positional encoding.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 4–5, Figure 3, Intent-Conditioned Dynamics Modeling, Eqs. (10)–(11); p. 10, Eqs. (18)–(27)
evidence.detail: The semantic-query/action-key mask block is negative infinity. Action queries read semantic and action keys/values; semantic queries read only semantic keys/values. Both streams attend to language/proprioception context. Semantic and action tokens use 3D and 1D RoPE respectively.

Independent Gaussian noise corrupts actions and semantic latents at a shared timestep. The detailed formulation predicts velocities targeting noise minus clean data, with an optional normalized SmoothL1 future-token head.

Current-observation semantic tokens are cached across action denoising steps; future semantic rollout is bypassed. Receding-horizon control executes the first R actions before observing again; numerical H and R are not supplied.

evidence.location: PDF p. 11, Model Architecture, Table 6, Eqs. (38)–(40)
evidence.detail: 384×384 frames produce 576 tokens of width 1664, compressed to width 96. ISAE encoder/decoder each have three blocks and 16 heads. Both DiTs have 30 layers, width 1664 and 24 heads. The semantic branch is initialized from Wan2.2-TI2V-5B with interpolation and scaling.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Implementation Details; p. 11, Table 7 and Training Objectives and Optimization, Eqs. (41)–(42)
evidence.detail: The main text specifies 24 NVIDIA H200 GPUs and global batch 256. ISAE/policy training takes 200k/400k steps with AdamW, learning rate 1e-4, weight decay 0.05, beta values 0.9/0.95, 5k warmup, cosine decay, bf16 and clipping 1.0. Table 7 sets action/semantic weights to 1/1 and the extra future weight to zero; schedulers use shift 5.0 and SIGReg uses 1024 projections.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 12–13, Training Paradigm, Stage I–III and Figure 7
evidence.detail: LoRA and a masked predictor adapt a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 ViT-G/16 backbone on a described five-source robot corpus, using third-person:wrist sampling 7:3. Adapted encoder and ISAE are frozen for final training. Stage II uses two-second windows and up to three views. Stage III describes frozen T5 conditioning, source-homogeneous batches and separate 7-DoF/14-DoF action heads.

evidence.location: PDF p. 11, Eqs. (41)–(42), Table 7; p. 12, Figure 6 and Eq. (44); p. 13, Eq. (46); p. 15, Table 9
evidence.detail: The implementation section gives two unit-weight velocity losses and zero extra future loss. Page 12 instead describes SmoothL1 between predicted semantic velocity and target V-JEPA features, with action/JEPA weights 1/0.1. Page 13 describes a latent future-token SmoothL1 loss with weights 0.1/1. Table 9 labels future prediction weight 0.2. No reconciliation is supplied.

evidence.location: PDF p. 12, Figure 6 and Training and Inference; p. 10, Eqs. (23)–(25); p. 13, Stage III
evidence.detail: Figure 6 shows semantic K/V and action Q on the left and a frozen V-JEPA/ISAE cache on the right. Its training-only box contains an ISAE label although ISAE remains at inference and is frozen in Stage III. The figure uses a Cross-Attn abstraction; the detailed formulation uses joint masked self-attention that also includes action keys/values.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Experimental Setup; p. 14, Table 8 caption
evidence.detail: RoboTwin 2.0 has 50 tasks and uses 27.5K mixed clean/randomized demonstrations. LIBERO and LIBERO-plus are described as 40 tasks and 2,000 evaluation episodes with zero-shot perturbation transfer. Table 8 states 100 trials per RoboTwin task and condition.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Table 1, LeapBot-WA, Fast-WAM, Lingbot-VA and Qwen-RobotManip rows
evidence.detail: LeapBot-WA reports 91.04% clean, 92.48% randomized and 91.76% average. Fast-WAM reports 91.85% average; Lingbot-VA 92.24%; Qwen-RobotManip 93.85%. LeapBot-WA has the best randomized score among the listed WAMs and is marked without embodied pretraining.

evidence.location: PDF p. 14, Table 8, Average/Open Laptop/Pick Dual Bottles rows and Evaluation on RoboTwin Benchmark prose; p. 5, Table 1
evidence.detail: Table 8 repeats LeapBot-WA's 91.04/92.48 values but prose says 92.64/89.80. Prose claims perfect Open Laptop and Pick Dual Bottles success, while table values are 99/97 and 97/98. Baseline averages differ from Table 1, and an ellipsis replaces many task rows.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 2 and Simulation Results paragraph
evidence.detail: LeapBot-WA reports Spatial/Object/Goal/LIBERO-10 success 96.2/99.6/97.6/95.6 and average 97.3%. The prose instead says 97.1%. JEPA-VLA averages 96.4%, VLA-JEPA 96.1%, PALM 94.5%, and Lingbot-VA/Cosmos-Policy 98.5%.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 3, all columns
evidence.detail: LIBERO-Plus averages are LeapBot-WA 73.1%, VLA-JEPA 62.9%, JEPA-VLA 25.6%, Cosmos-Policy 82.2% and ImageWAM 83.1%. LeapBot-WA scores Camera 33.8, Robot 75.1, Language 87.8, Light 93.4, Background 90.1, Noise 54.7 and Layout 76.7. Some bold entries are below other displayed values.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 4 and Performance Analysis of Architectural Components
evidence.detail: Across baseline, Robot-Mix JEPA, ISAE without SIGReg and full ISAE, averages are 89.4/91.2/91.4/92.0 and LIBERO-10 scores 74.2/81.0/80.2/85.0. Adding SIGReg changes Goal from 92.4 to 89.2. No seed variation or link to the Table 2 configuration is supplied.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 14–15, Ablation Analysis of World-Action Components and Table 9
evidence.detail: No semantic context averages 47.7%; static semantic context with zero future weight averages 90.7%; future prediction weight 0.2 averages 92.0%. The latter two LIBERO-10 values are 78.4 and 85.0. The exact relationship to the other loss descriptions is unresolved.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Figure 4 and Analysis of Hardware Efficiency
evidence.detail: Figure 4 labels LeapBot-WA 2.9B parameters/546 ms, Fast-WAM 6.0B/486 ms, Cosmos-Policy 2.1B/1413 ms, Lingbot-VA 5.5B/4482 ms, and Motus 8.0B/3231 ms. The figure and discussion do not define a matched inference hardware, denoising-step or action-horizon protocol.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 5 and Cross-Domain Transfer and Representation Quality
evidence.detail: Base versus mixed-domain JEPA action MSE is 0.0437/0.0417, dynamics MSE 0.00496/0.00308 and proprioception MSE 0.00460/0.00329. Relative reductions are reported as 4.6%, 37.9% and 28.5%; probe split and fitting details are not specified here.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 5–6, Real-World Deployment, Real-World Results and Figure 5
evidence.detail: UR5 pick-and-place examples involve fruits, vegetables and containers under changed textures and lighting. The reported real-world evidence is qualitative; no trial count, success-rate table or matched physical baseline is provided.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 7–8, Conclusion and Limitations
evidence.detail: The authors identify dependence on foundation representations and difficulty with fine contact physics and high-frequency tactile interactions. Multimodal anchors and long-horizon planning are future work.

evidence.location: PDF p. 15, Qualitative Results and Visualizations; pp. 16–18, Figures 8–10
evidence.detail: Figures show paired external/wrist LIBERO views, perturbed LIBERO-Plus scenes, and five RoboTwin execution sequences. These selected images do not measure attention shifts, prove invariance or rule out memorization.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 3–4, Eqs. (4)–(7); pp. 11–13, Implementation Details and Training Paradigm
evidence.detail: The PDF supplies ISAE dimensions, optimizer details and some view sampling choices, but not numerical cosine/isotropy/KL-maximum weights, a complete five-source data manifest, LoRA rank or adaptation duration, action normalization, exact cache projection implementation, software versions, or a full evaluation configuration.
